get.description:
Whether ABHA flows are available, without attempting a call.

Deliberately does not touch ABDM: the frontend asks this on load to
decide whether to render the identity flow at all, and that decision
should not depend on the sandbox being up.

schema.title: Response Abha Status Api Abha Status Get

post.description:
First request, or a resend when `txnId` is present.

The resend budget is spent *before* the call goes out, not after it
succeeds: a refusal from ABDM still consumed an OTP send on their side,
so counting only successes would let a loop of failures sail past the
limit the checklist requires.

schema.title: Response Api Enrol Mobile Verify Api Abha Enrol Mobile Verify Post
Response Api Address Suggestions Api Abha Enrol Address Suggestions Get
Response Api Set Address Api Abha Enrol Address Post

get.description:
One poll, not a blocking wait.

`faceauth.await_capture` blocks until the patient acts, which is right
for a script and wrong for an HTTP handler -- it would hold a worker for
up to ten minutes per patient. The browser polls this instead.

schema.title: Response Api Face Status Api Abha Face Status Get

get.description:
Resend budget and countdown for one transaction.

Read-only, so polling it is free. It exists so the UI renders its
countdown from the authority that enforces the limit rather than keeping
a second timer that can disagree with the first.

post.description:
`null` means no such address -- a branch for the UI, not an error.

NHA's checklist requires the "not found" case to offer ABHA creation
(VRFY_ABHA_302), so it must be distinguishable from a failure.

schema.title: Response Api Address Search Api Abha Address Search Post

post.description:
The X-token this returns only works against the PHR host -- pass
`viaAbhaAddress=true` to /profile and /card when using it.

schema.title: Response Api Search Api Abha Search Get
Response Api Qr Api Abha Qr Get
Response Api Card Api Abha Card Get

post.description:
Tag one verified ABHA number to one patient.

The patient is looked up before the link is written. A tag pointing at a
patient_id that does not exist is worse than no tag: it reads as a
verified identity and resolves to nothing.

get.description: Check before creating a patient record -- the checklist's actual ask.

schema.title: Response Api Link By Abha Api Abha Link By Abha  Abha Number  Get
Response Api Link By Patient Api Abha Link By Patient  Patient Id  Get
Response Api Unlink Api Abha Link  Abha Number  Delete

post.description:
Re-read the same file and write only the approved facts.

The file is uploaded again rather than cached between the two calls. That
costs a second OCR pass and buys statelessness: there is no server-side
extraction sitting around half-approved, and no cache key to get wrong in
a way that commits one patient's facts against another's id.

Fact ids are deterministic over (file, page, line, code), so the second
pass reproduces exactly the ids the reviewer saw -- and any that it does
not reproduce are reported rather than written.

get.description: List patients, optionally filtered by a case-insensitive name substring.

schema.title: Response Api List Patients Api Patients Get

post.description:
Conversational RAG: NER + retrieval, same as /api/query, plus
conversation memory and a Groq-generated reply instead of the fixed
template. See backend/conversation.py.

AbhaAccount.title: AbhaAccount
AbhaAccount.description:
One ABHA identity, as returned by search, login and enrolment.

`mobile` being `None` is meaningful, not missing data -- see
`EnrolmentResult.mobile_is_linked`.

AbhaProfile.title: AbhaProfile
AbhaProfile.description:
The full profile from `GET /v3/profile/account`, which is richer than
the account stub returned by search.

AddressOtpChannel.title: AddressOtpChannel
AddressOtpChannel.description:
Where the OTP for an ABHA-address verification is sent.

AADHAAR -- UIDAI sends it to the Aadhaar-linked mobile (VRFY_ABHA_102).
MOBILE  -- ABDM sends it to the ABHA-linked communication mobile
           (VRFY_ABHA_202).

Brief.title: Brief
Brief.description:
The rendered answer.

`sections` is always the deterministic template output. The optional LLM
polish pass writes `prose` and flips `source`; it never edits or replaces
`sections`, so the grounded version survives a bad rewrite and the demo
works with the flag off.

BriefLine.title: BriefLine
BriefLine.description:
One rendered line, carrying the fact ids that justify it.

Provenance is not optional: the UI resolves these back to source
resources on click.

BriefSection.title: BriefSection
BriefSection.description:
A titled group of lines.

`empty_note` carries the explicit negative -- "No allergy records on
file." -- so an empty section still says something.

ChatRequest.title: ChatRequest
ChatRequest.description:
POST /api/chat. ``conversation_id`` omitted or null starts a new
conversation; passing one back threads the next turn onto it.

ChatResponse.title: ChatResponse
ChatResponse.description:
What POST /api/chat returns.

Same NER (`parse_query`) and retrieval (`retrieve`) as `/api/query` --
`result` here is the same `RetrievalResult` shape, so nothing that
already renders one needs a second code path. `answer` is the
conversational reply; `cited_fact_ids` is every fact and narrative chunk
that was actually shown to the model for this turn, not a parse of its
output -- provenance the same way `BriefLine.fact_ids` is, attached to
what was surfaced rather than claimed after the fact.

EnrolmentResult.title: EnrolmentResult
EnrolmentResult.description:
The outcome of `enrol/byAadhaar`.

`is_new` distinguishes a created ABHA from one that already existed --
ABDM answers both with 200 and the same body shape, differing only in
`new`/`isNew`. A caller that cannot tell them apart will report a
duplicate as a fresh enrolment.

EntityFacts.title: EntityFacts
EntityFacts.description:
Facts retrieved for one resolved entity.

Kept per-entity rather than merged into one pile because entities can
share a span: `aspirin` resolves to both an ALLERGY substance and four
MEDICATION products, and those are two different clinical answers.

Fact.title: Fact
Fact.description:
One row of facts.jsonl, mirroring the ingestion schema exactly.

Provenance fields (`source_resource_type`, `source_resource_id`,
`encounter_id`, `also_in`) are part of the record, not decoration: the UI
shows them on click and the brief cites `fact_id` for every line.

LoginMethod.title: LoginMethod
LoginMethod.description:
The three credentials the ABHA host accepts.

ABHA *address* is deliberately absent. It looks like it belongs here and
it does not: the ABHA host rejects it with "Invalid Scope" and "Invalid
Login Hint", because address verification is a separate family on the PHR
host. It lives in `abha/phr.py`. Adding a fourth row here is the mistake
that module's docstring exists to prevent.

LoginResult.title: LoginResult
LoginResult.description:
The outcome of `login/verify`.

One credential can map to several ABHA accounts -- ABDM allows six ABHA
numbers per mobile -- so this carries either a finished session (`token`
set, one account) or a choice to put to the user (`t_token` set,
`accounts` populated). `needs_account_selection` is the discriminator;
branching on `len(accounts)` alone is wrong, because a single-account
response still lists that account.

MatchQuality.title: MatchQuality
MatchQuality.description:
How an entity span was resolved to codes.

The downstream router branches on this, so an honest ``UNRESOLVED``
is more useful than a plausible-looking wrong code.

MissingItem.title: MissingItem
MissingItem.description:
Something a pre-op assessment expects to see that is not on file.

A set difference over coded facts, not a model. The product
differentiator is naming what is absent, so this is a first-class result
field rather than a footnote.

NarrativeMatch.title: NarrativeMatch
NarrativeMatch.description:
One hit from the REPORT-note vector-search fallback.

Stage 2 only, and a fallback only: ``retrieve()`` attempts this path
solely when nothing in the query resolved to a code at all. Never a
replacement for coded retrieval -- REPORT is the ~5% of the corpus with
no code to filter on, everything else stays on the structured path.

OcrFactOut.title: OcrFactOut
OcrFactOut.description: A proposed fact. Carries its own evidence so the UI can show why.

OtpChallenge.title: OtpChallenge
OtpChallenge.description:
The txnId returned by any `request/otp` call, plus what to show a user.

`masked_identifier` is ABDM's own masking of the destination
(`XXXXXXX769`). It exists so a UI can say *where* the OTP went without
this service ever holding the full number.

ParsedQuery.title: ParsedQuery
ParsedQuery.description: The parsed form of a doctor's natural-language question.

PatientSummary.title: PatientSummary
PatientSummary.description:
One row of patients.jsonl. The underscore-prefixed source keys are
aliased to clean names; both spellings are accepted on input.

QueryResponse.title: QueryResponse
QueryResponse.description:
What POST /api/query returns.

`parsed` is included so the UI can render the question with its resolved
entities highlighted by match quality -- the NER work is visible rather
than invisible.

ResolvedEntity.title: ResolvedEntity
ResolvedEntity.description: One span of the query, resolved (or not) to corpus codes.

RetrievalOutcome.title: RetrievalOutcome
RetrievalOutcome.description:
Why an entity's fact list looks the way it does.

The distinction this enum exists for: an empty `FOUND_NONE` means the
patient genuinely has nothing on file, which is a clinical finding.
`NOT_RETRIEVED` means we never asked, which is not.

RetrievalResult.title: RetrievalResult
RetrievalResult.description: Everything the retrieval stage found, and everything it did not.

StageTimings.title: StageTimings
StageTimings.description:
Per-stage latency as structured fields, not log lines.

Populated as the request moves through the pipeline; a stage that did not
run stays None. `vector_ms` is reserved for stage 2 and stays None until
the Pinecone path exists.
